professional: a family-entertainment-center operator or a small-business lender's credit analyst who underwrites trampoline park / FEC loans and would first check the cost stack (management payroll, ramp-up, party-room capacity) and whether payback and break-even are computed on a defensible basis

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` (24 pass) and a scratch script (scratchpad r.mjs) on sampleInput(). Recomputed in independent Python (not the author's code or tests): slots 14,560, visits 2,912, revenue $88,864, staff $32,104.80, fixed $63,304.80, profit $9,311.92, margin 10.48%, payback 64.43 months, break-even fill 16.6445% all match the engine to the cent. Loan payment: 100,000 at 6% over 60 months gives $1,933.28 from the textbook annuity formula (and the engine's 12%/12 case gives the standard 8,884.88). Round trips: typing minTicket ($21.98) back gives margin 0.2000; minPaybackTicket ($19.18) gives payback 48.0000; profit at break-even fill is 1.5e-11. Edge: 100% financed $1M build gives loan $20,111/month, profit -$10,799, plausible. Arithmetic is right; the limit is the model, see domain.
evidence.completeness: Checked every feature in README/VENTURE.yaml: monthly profit and margin (works), payback (works), break-even fill (works), lowest ticket for target margin and for payback (works, round-trips), 10%/20% sensitivity (works), two-scenario comparison (works, errors prefixed Scenario B), copy/CSV/save/load (resultText, resultCsv, serializeState/parseState exercised by tests and round-trip), usage opt-out (usage.test.mjs). Served page https://marisstella.app/trampoline-park-profit-calculator/ returned 200 and the guide page resolves (307 to the clean URL, then served). No TODOs or stubs found. Not exercised: the browser UI itself, since no headless browser was run; page.test.mjs only regex-checks index.html.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture: 24 pass, 0 fail, about 0.2 s. Five hand-seeded mutations: (1) drop reserve from the min-ticket divisor: caught (2 fail). (2) validation bound 100 to 1000: caught (1 fail). (3) sensitivity payback ignores the loan (`op = sp + payment` to `op = sp`): NOT caught, 24 pass. (4) party-share warning threshold 0.35 to 0.95: NOT caught. (5) 5-year payback note threshold 60 to 600: NOT caught. The worked-example, break-even and min-ticket tests are strong (random-room round trips), but sensitivity payback figures, all of buildNotes, and compareScenarios winners are untested in value (the compare test only asserts the winner is one of A/B/tie).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (232 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs head, index.html script. Clean pure-function engine, input validation with bounds, no network calls (tested), closed-form break-even from linearity, tolerance handled in meets/meetsPayback. Defects: blank input fields become 0 via Number('') in readMap (index.html:159) so an emptied fill or rent silently solves instead of erroring; SESSION_HOURS 1.75 is a hard-coded constant not exposed to the user; profitAt recomputes fixedCosts and loan each call (minor). The engine is not duplicated in the page.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer, no-warranty, privacy and non-affiliation text are on index.html and the guide and are asserted by page.test.mjs. 'Hundreds of random parks' test claim is backed (300 draws each, asserted checked > 100). Guide worked-example numbers are tested against the engine. Not backed by any file: build cost 'roughly $250,000 to $800,000' (index FAQ), 'a realistic 20.0% filled' (guide intro), parties 'often a quarter or more of revenue', break-even fill 'lower than most owners guess', 'Most lenders and landlords want to see less than five' years (calc.mjs:148), 'Weekday school-term fill is usually the part that disappoints'. VENTURE.yaml header cites $300k-$1M and 15-30k sq ft with no source. Served llms.txt and sitemap carry the marisstella.app host (source github.io host is rewritten at deploy), so no URL defect.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a prospective owner testing a lease: enter capacity, sessions, fill, ticket, parties, staff, rent, build; get profit, payback, break-even fill and ticket needed. It completes in one pass and the sensitivity output answers the main fear (fill shortfall). Gaps an owner hits in the first hour: no general manager / owner salary line (floor staff only), no opening ramp-up (year-one fill is lower), jumpers in party rooms are not netted from the slots, sales tax and income tax absent, payback is before tax and before the loan, session length is fixed at 1.75 h.
evidence.domain: Compared against how FEC/trampoline park pro formas and SBA-style lender models are built (per-capita revenue, labour as percent of revenue with manager salaries, occupancy cost, EBITDA and debt-service coverage). Departures: no DSCR (a lender's first metric), no ramp-up or seasonality, staff cost is hours open times floor staff only (no pre-open/close or management hours), a single uniform fill across weekday and weekend, payback on pre-tax operating profit with no working capital. It states it is arithmetic on typed numbers and refuses to give benchmarks beyond a few unsourced ranges, which is honest but leaves the number only as good as the inputs.

Cost model has floor staff only: no general manager or owner salary, no opening ramp-up, no DSCR, so profit and payback read optimistic against how a lender underwrites an FEC
Party guests occupy jump capacity but parties are added on top of walk-in fill, and party count is not checked against rooms (only a note), so revenue can double count slots

VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype while the README and page present a finished tool; session length 1.75 h is a fixed constant users cannot change

verdict: The arithmetic is right: every headline output (slots, visits, revenue, staff cost, profit, margin, payback, break-even fill, loan payment) matches an independent Python recompute, and the lowest-ticket outputs round-trip to their targets exactly. It does not meet the bar because verification (2) and claims (2) are below 3: three of five seeded mutations survived, including the loan being charged against sensitivity payback, and several industry figures on the pages have no source. A lender or park operator would also find the model optimistic (no manager payroll, no ramp-up, no DSCR, party guests not netted from capacity). It is finished against its own README (completeness 3) but a prototype-grade planning tool for real lease decisions. The browser UI itself was not driven; the page was only confirmed to be served (HTTP 200).
